scope: Topic library cleanup: fields written for the retired NeuroEngineering Atlas iOS app (Swift/SwiftUI mini-project ideas, labs that were never built, SF Symbols icon names) removed from topics and subjects. Nothing rendered them; accentHex stays for subject card accents.

changes.before: Mock a BCI loop in Swift: random spike rates → moving average preprocessor → linear decoder → 2D cursor on screen.
CursorBCI Decoder Lab — interactively drive a cursor with simulated neural features.
Implement a 2D Kalman cursor decoder fed by synthetic cosine-tuned 'neurons'; render the cursor in SwiftUI.
CursorBCI Decoder Lab — VR target-acquisition tasks with a live decoder.
Pick a hypothetical neuro device (e.g., a closed-loop tinnitus mask). Map out which pathway fits and what evidence you'd need.
No future lab — strictly clinical/regulatory; pairs well with all neurodevice subjects.
Make a SwiftUI flowchart UI that walks a user through a DBS troubleshooting tree, branching on impedance and symptom reproducibility.
No future lab — clinical workflow only.
Simulate a noisy biomarker. Implement a threshold detector and an adaptive controller; measure false positives vs. missed events.
Closed-Loop Stimulation Lab — interactively tune detector thresholds and see therapy outcomes.
Implement line length and band power features on simulated seizure-like data; compare detection latency and false alarm rates.
Closed-Loop Stimulation Lab — race a detector against a propagating seizure visualization.
Simulate a 2-population rate model (excitatory and inhibitory) in Swift; plot its response to step input under different gains.
No future lab specific to this — pairs well with SignalScope Lab visualizations.
Implement HH in Swift; plot voltage and gating variables during a single spike.
No direct future lab — supports DBS Circuit Lab indirectly.
Generate synthetic cosine-tuned neurons and fit a ridge regression decoder; sweep the ridge penalty and plot generalization.
CursorBCI Decoder Lab — compare a linear and non-linear decoder on the same task.
Train a decoder twice — once with random shuffling, once with chronological split. Report both numbers and explain the gap.
CursorBCI Decoder Lab — induce overfitting on purpose and watch real-time control degrade.
Mock a consent UI: show what data the device records, why, and how long it's kept; let the user opt in/out per category.
No specific lab — every NeuroSim Lab will share these design defaults.
Design a SwiftUI 'patient dashboard' that surfaces what a closed-loop device just did and why, with clear off and override controls.
Closed-Loop Stimulation Lab — show the patient's view of the device's decisions in VR.
Make a SwiftUI calculator that takes electrode area and material, outputs safe charge injection limits.
SignalScope Lab — visualize what each electrode type can and can't see.
Plot synthetic spike amplitude vs. days post-implant under different 'response severity' coefficients; explore what coatings do.
SignalScope Lab — simulate how recordings degrade over time.
Simulate a leaky integrate-and-fire neuron in Swift Playgrounds: integrate input current, fire a spike when voltage crosses threshold, then reset.
SignalScope Lab — record and visualize simulated action potentials in 3D.
Take a sample neural recording (or a generated one), apply a high-pass and low-pass filter, and plot spikes vs. LFP side by side.
SignalScope Lab — flip filter settings live and watch how the same recording becomes spikes or LFPs.
Make a SwiftUI animation that overlays a slow hemodynamic curve on top of a fast neural firing trace to show the temporal mismatch.
No direct lab — pairs with Closed-Loop Stimulation Lab when discussing biomarker speed.
Build a SwiftUI map of brain regions; clicking a region 'lesions' it and toggles which functions are listed as impaired.
No direct lab — informs DBS Circuit Lab targeting choices.
Design a SwiftUI control panel that mixes intent (from a slider) with autonomy (auto-grasp toggle) for a virtual 2-DOF arm.
Prosthetic Grip Lab — VR pick-and-place tasks driven by simulated decoder intent.
Prototype a sensory-feedback map in SwiftUI: as virtual fingers press, illuminate a corresponding zone on a body diagram.
Prosthetic Grip Lab — toggle feedback on/off and time pick-and-place tasks.
Build a programming-session simulator: slider for amplitude, pulse width, frequency; mock side-effect zones light up as values exceed thresholds.
DBS Circuit Lab — visualize current spread from a lead in 3D anatomy.
Code a 2D map of induced currents under a figure-8 coil for a few coil orientations; compare focality.
DBS Circuit Lab — TMS extension: visualize induced E-fields on a brain mesh.
Build a SwiftUI game where the user 'practices' a movement (slider/gesture) and earns adaptive difficulty as accuracy climbs.
Prosthetic Grip Lab and CursorBCI Decoder Lab share the rehabilitation feedback patterns.
Simulate a fatigue model: stimulate at a fixed rate, track force output declining over time, then try interleaved stimulation to delay fatigue.
